analysis.summary: A single Horizon Europe Innovation Action of about €43 million to develop, validate and demonstrate wave and tidal energy technology, covering survival in harsh seas, moorings, foundations, condition monitoring and the use of AI. It opens on 3 December 2026 and closes on 31 March 2027; you would join as a partner rather than lead.

topic_fit.notes: Squarely your field: wave and tidal energy systems that survive a harsh ocean environment, with moorings, foundations, test-tank validation and AI in technology development all named in scope.

career_stage.notes: A €43 million multi-country demonstration programme needs an established coordinator, so you could not lead it. The realistic role is partner, contributing wave-loading and survivability modelling, tank testing or machine-learning methods.

eligibility.notes: The brief sets no restriction beyond the standard Horizon Europe country rules, under which UK universities can take part and be funded because the UK is an associated country. Confirm in General Annex B and with Manchester's research office.

analysis.why_fit: The topic is your own field, and partner roles in consortia that need ocean and fluids expertise are something you asked for. If you miss the consortium, the winning project must run its own funding calls for third parties, including universities, with up to €800,000 per third party for projects of about 12-18 months.
analysis.concerns: Only one grant is expected, so everything depends on being in the winning consortium, and bids of this size are usually assembled well before the call opens. The core consortium must deliver at least three distinct demonstration activities up to TRL 7, each with a convincing route to permits and financial close, so partners are chosen for what they add to those.
analysis.recommend_reason: Core topic and a partner role you want, with a fall-back through the project's later third-party calls; worth a few weeks of effort if you can get into a credible consortium quickly.

The 2026 round closed on 16 July 2026; the scheme runs yearly, so expect a 2027 call, though its timing moved from January-April in 2025 to May-July in 2026.

topic_fit.notes: Any science area within NERC's remit is eligible, and your work on ocean waves, wave breaking and coastal hydrodynamics is physical oceanography that should sit inside it. Most of the project must be NERC remit, so lead with the ocean and coastal science rather than structural loading.

career_stage.notes: NERC welcomes applicants at any career stage, and a small two-year partnership grant is a realistic size for an early-career principal investigator.

eligibility.notes: You are at a UK organisation eligible for NERC funding in a qualifying role. You may be on only one application, cannot apply in two consecutive years or while holding a live seedcorn grant, and the partner must be genuinely new to you under NERC's tests.

analysis.why_fit: It matches your wish for an international collaboration award you can lead without a huge application: it pays for exchange visits, workshops and proof-of-concept work with an overseas group whose data, facilities or field sites you cannot get in the UK. Extreme-wave field measurements or a wave basin abroad would be natural hooks, and a partner in Taiwan or São Paulo can bring co-funding from NSTC or FAPESP.
analysis.concerns: The 'new partner' rule is strict: no joint funding, no paper where one of you is lead author with the other as co-author, no more than two co-authored papers, and no former lab colleagues, supervisors or students. A project that reads as engineering rather than environmental science risks failing the remit check, and the fund will not pay for conference attendance, PhD studentships or the partner's salary.
analysis.recommend_reason: A modest application for a grant you can lead at your stage that funds exactly the kind of new international link you are looking for, provided you frame it as ocean and coastal science.

opportunities.title: Exploring the frontiers of environmental research 2026

analysis.summary: NERC's small-grant call for early-stage, high-risk, curiosity-driven environmental research: £100,000–£200,000 full economic cost over up to two years, with a reduced expectation of preliminary data and assessment by distributed peer review. The 2026 round closed on 12 November 2026, so treat this as one to prepare for the next round, which the year in the title suggests will run in autumn 2027.

topic_fit.notes: Any topic is welcome if it sits predominantly within NERC's remit and addresses a clearly defined environmental science question; rogue waves, wave breaking and coastal hydrodynamics can be framed that way (NERC's discipline list includes ocean–atmosphere interactions, land–ocean interactions and regional weather and extreme events). Engineering-led work such as wave loads on structures would more likely fall to EPSRC.

career_stage.notes: NERC encourages applications from all career stages and says it judges capability to lead rather than length in post. A two-year project of £100,000–£200,000 that needs no preliminary data is a realistic size for a new lecturer to lead.

eligibility.notes: You meet the stated rules for a project lead (UK resident, affiliated with an eligible UK research organisation) and may appear on at most two applications, leading only one. Before the next round, confirm that your idea is NERC-led rather than EPSRC-led and read the individual-level demand-management rule, whose details are not in the brief.

analysis.why_fit: It pays for exactly the kind of risky first test a new group needs — for example an equation-discovery or machine-learning route into rogue-wave or wave-breaking physics — at a size you can lead alone and without needing preliminary data. Success would also give you a footing with NERC alongside your EPSRC award.
analysis.concerns: The work must be predominantly NERC science, so an engineering-flavoured proposal risks being judged out of remit. You must cost at least 0.2 FTE of your own time and review six to eight other applications within 15 working days (failing to do so means automatic rejection), and the 2027 dates are only an estimate from a single round.
analysis.recommend_reason: Open-topic, welcoming to early-career leads and moderate in effort, with an ocean-science framing that suits your wave work; get an idea and a remit check ready ahead of the expected autumn 2027 round.
